title: Computer-aided detection lowers adenoma miss rate in tandem colonoscopy
summary: In a prospective tandem study at one Chinese centre, 369 patients were randomly assigned to computer-aided detection (CADe) colonoscopy first or routine white-light colonoscopy first, each followed by the other procedure. The adenoma miss rate was 13.89% with CADe versus 40.00% with routine colonoscopy. The study is single-centre.
ai_technology: Deep learning computer-aided detection (CADe) for real-time colonoscopy

evidence.tested: Adenoma miss rate of CADe versus routine colonoscopy in a randomized prospective tandem design (n = 369).
evidence.unknown: Single centre; adenoma miss rate is not a long-term clinical outcome; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning system alerting endoscopists to polyps in real time.
